title: Foreslå en plan og bli enige om tidspunkt — suggest a plan and agree on a time
goal: Propose an activity, respond to availability, offer one alternative, and state the agreed plan.

objectives.statement: Propose an activity, respond to availability, offer one alternative, and state the agreed plan.

spans.value: Mina and Jonas want to meet at the weekend. Mina suggests an activity, but her first proposed time does not work for Jonas.
Skal vi gå på kafé på lørdag?

blocks.translation: Shall we go to a café on Saturday?

spans.value: Ja, gjerne! Når passer det for deg?

blocks.translation: Yes, I’d love to! When works for you?

spans.value: Passer det klokka to?
Dessverre, jeg kan ikke klokka to. Jeg skal hjelpe søsteren min.

blocks.translation: Unfortunately, I can’t at two o’clock. I’m going to help my sister.

spans.value: Hva med klokka fire?
Ja, det passer fint.
Flott! Da møtes vi på Kafé Sol klokka fire på lørdag.

blocks.translation: Great! Then we’ll meet at Café Sol at four o’clock on Saturday.

spans.value: Det gjør vi. Vi ses!
Mina and Jonas complete four useful steps:

items.value: Jonas responds positively but asks about the time.
Jonas cannot manage the first time, so Mina offers an alternative.
They state the final plan clearly.

spans.value: An informal plan often takes only a few lines, but both people need to know what they are doing and when they are meeting.
A common way to suggest doing something together is:

no.value: Skal vi + activity?

en.value: Shall we + activity?

spans.value: In this expression, skal vi does not sound like a formal obligation. It is a friendly proposal.

no.value: Skal vi ta en kaffe?

en.value: Shall we have a coffee?

no.value: Skal vi gå en tur etter jobb?

en.value: Shall we go for a walk after work?

no.value: Skal vi se en film på fredag?

en.value: Shall we watch a film on Friday?

no.value: Skal vi lage middag sammen?

en.value: Shall we make dinner together?

spans.value: You can include a day or time in the proposal:

no.value: Skal vi spise lunsj sammen i morgen?

en.value: Shall we have lunch together tomorrow?

no.value: Skal vi møtes på søndag formiddag?

en.value: Shall we meet on Sunday morning?

spans.value: Another natural proposal begins with hva med, meaning how about:

no.value: Hva med en tur i parken?

en.value: How about a walk in the park?

no.value: Hva med å dra på kino på lørdag?

en.value: How about going to the cinema on Saturday?

spans.value: Use
hva med + noun
for a thing or event:

no.value: Hva med en kaffe?

en.value: How about a coffee?

spans.value: Use
hva med å + verb
for an activity:

no.value: Hva med å ta en kaffe?

en.value: How about having a coffee?

spans.value: In the opening dialogue, Mina first uses skal vi to propose the main activity. Later, she uses hva med to suggest a different time.
Checkpoint: Recognize the proposal
Read a short exchange between two friends and identify the sentence that proposes their activity. Then say what activity they may do and whether a day or time has already been mentioned.
If you like the proposal, you can respond briefly and warmly:

no.value: Ja, gjerne!

en.value: Yes, I’d love to!

no.value: Det høres hyggelig ut.

en.value: That sounds nice.

no.value: God idé!

en.value: Good idea!

no.value: Ja, det kan vi gjøre.

en.value: Yes, we can do that.

spans.value: These responses accept the activity, but they do not always settle the time. Compare:

no.value: Ja, gjerne!

en.value: Yes, I’d love to!

spans.value: This accepts the activity.

no.value: Ja, gjerne! Klokka tre passer fint.

en.value: Yes, I’d love to! Three o’clock works well.

spans.value: This accepts both the activity and the proposed time.
You can also accept the activity while showing that the proposed time is difficult:

no.value: Jeg blir gjerne med, men jeg kan ikke på fredag.

en.value: I’d be happy to come along, but I can’t on Friday.

no.value: Det høres hyggelig ut, men klokka seks passer ikke.

en.value: That sounds nice, but six o’clock doesn’t work.

spans.value: This distinction is important. You may want to meet even when you cannot accept the first suggested time.
The verb passe is very useful when agreeing on a time. In scheduling, it means to suit or to work.

no.value: Passer det klokka to?

en.value: Does two o’clock work?

no.value: Ja, det passer fint.

en.value: Yes, that works well.

no.value: Nei, det passer dessverre ikke.

en.value: No, unfortunately that doesn’t work.

spans.value: You can ask about a day in the same way:

no.value: Passer det på torsdag?

en.value: Does Thursday work?

no.value: Passer lørdag for deg?

en.value: Does Saturday work for you?

spans.value: To ask more generally, say:

no.value: Når passer det for deg?

en.value: When works for you?

spans.value: To state your availability, kan is often enough:

no.value: Jeg kan etter jobb.

en.value: I’m available after work.

no.value: Jeg kan på søndag.

en.value: I’m available on Sunday.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke før klokka fem.

en.value: I’m not available before five o’clock.

spans.value: Here kan means that the time is possible for you in this situation. It does not describe a learned ability.
Compare:

no.value: Jeg kan møtes klokka fem.

en.value: I can meet at five o’clock.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke møtes klokka fem.

en.value: I can’t meet at five o’clock.

spans.value: The second response is clear, but an informal conversation often sounds more cooperative if you add an alternative.
Checkpoint: Respond to availability
Return to Mina and Jonas. Imagine that Mina proposes the café and suggests two o’clock. Give Jonas a response that shows he likes the activity but cannot meet at that time.
When the first time does not work, offer another possible time. This keeps the conversation moving toward an agreement.
A simple pattern is:

no.value: Hva med + alternative time?

en.value: How about + alternative time?

no.value: Hva med klokka fire?

en.value: How about four o’clock?

no.value: Hva med søndag i stedet?

en.value: How about Sunday instead?

no.value: Hva med litt senere?

en.value: How about a little later?

spans.value: You can also state your availability directly:

no.value: Jeg kan klokka fire.

en.value: I’m available at four o’clock.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke på lørdag, men jeg kan på søndag.

en.value: I can’t on Saturday, but I’m available on Sunday.

no.value: Fredag passer ikke. Kan vi møtes på torsdag?

en.value: Friday doesn’t work. Can we meet on Thursday?

spans.value: The word i stedet means instead and makes the contrast explicit:

no.value: Kan vi møtes klokka seks i stedet?

en.value: Can we meet at six o’clock instead?

no.value: Jeg kan ikke i kveld. Hva med i morgen i stedet?

en.value: I can’t tonight. How about tomorrow instead?

spans.value: For this lesson, one clear alternative is enough. Avoid producing a long list of possible times before the other person has had a chance to respond.
An aligned contrast
Rejecting without helping

no.value: Nei, jeg kan ikke.

en.value: No, I can’t.

spans.value: This is understandable, but the other person must make another suggestion.
Rejecting and offering an alternative

no.value: Jeg kan ikke klokka to, men jeg kan klokka fire.

en.value: I can’t at two, but I’m available at four.

spans.value: This response helps both people reach an agreement.
Offering the alternative as a question

no.value: Klokka to passer ikke. Hva med klokka fire?

en.value: Two o’clock doesn’t work. How about four?

spans.value: This sounds friendly and gives the other person space to accept or reject the new time.
Checkpoint: Supply one alternative

Use a situation in which a friend suggests going for a walk on Saturday morning, but you are busy then. Respond positively to the activity, say that Saturday morning does not work, and offer one alternative time.
Combine a proposal, an availability response, and exactly one cooperative alternative.

sections.title: Agreeing and stating the final plan

spans.value: Once both people accept the activity and time, state the agreed plan. This prevents confusion.
In the opening dialogue, Mina says:

no.value: Da møtes vi på Kafé Sol klokka fire på lørdag.

en.value: Then we’ll meet at Café Sol at four o’clock on Saturday.

spans.value: Here da means then or in that case. It shows that the plan follows from the agreement.
Useful confirmation patterns include:

no.value: Da møtes vi klokka seks.

en.value: Then we’ll meet at six o’clock.

no.value: Da tar vi en kaffe etter jobb.

en.value: Then we’ll have a coffee after work.

no.value: Flott, da sees vi på søndag.

en.value: Great, then we’ll see each other on Sunday.

no.value: Supert! Da går vi på kino fredag kveld.

en.value: Great! Then we’ll go to the cinema on Friday evening.

spans.value: A complete confirmation usually repeats the activity and the agreed time:

no.value: Da spiser vi lunsj sammen klokka ett på torsdag.

en.value: Then we’ll have lunch together at one o’clock on Thursday.

spans.value: This is clearer than a response such as OK or flott on its own.
The other person can confirm with:

no.value: Ja, det gjør vi.

en.value: Yes, we will.

no.value: Det passer fint. Vi ses da!

en.value: That works well. See you then!

no.value: Flott, vi ses på lørdag!

en.value: Great, see you on Saturday!

spans.value: Treating a time problem as rejection of the whole invitation

no.value: Nei, jeg vil ikke.

en.value: No, I don’t want to.

spans.value: This rejects the activity. Do not use it if you want to join but are unavailable at the proposed time.
Use:

no.value: Jeg blir gjerne med, men jeg kan ikke klokka tre.

en.value: I’d be happy to come along, but I can’t at three o’clock.

spans.value: Giving an unclear alternative

no.value: Kanskje en annen gang.

en.value: Maybe another time.

spans.value: This does not provide a usable time.
Use a specific alternative:

no.value: Hva med søndag ettermiddag?

en.value: How about Sunday afternoon?

spans.value: Accepting without confirming what was agreed

no.value: Ja, fint.

en.value: Yes, fine.

spans.value: This may be enough in a very short conversation, but it can leave the plan unclear.
A clearer ending is:

no.value: Ja, fint. Da møtes vi utenfor kinoen klokka sju.

en.value: Yes, fine. Then we’ll meet outside the cinema at seven.

spans.value: Mixing two different times in the confirmation
If one person rejects two o’clock and both accept four o’clock, the final sentence must use four o’clock. The confirmation should repeat the latest agreed time, not the original proposal.
On Saturday afternoon, Jonas sends Mina a message.
Hei! Jeg er ferdig hos søsteren min klokka halv fire. Passer det fortsatt at vi møtes klokka fire?

blocks.translation: Hi! I’ll be finished at my sister’s at half past three. Does it still work for us to meet at four o’clock?

spans.value: Ja, det gjør det. Vi møtes på Kafé Sol klokka fire.

blocks.translation: Yes, it does. We’ll meet at Café Sol at four o’clock.

spans.value: Flott. Vi ses snart!
Vi ses!
Mina repeats the place and time, so Jonas knows that nothing has changed. The short exchange closes the same plan introduced at the beginning of the chapter.
Checkpoint: Build the complete exchange

Create a short message exchange between two named friends. One person proposes an informal activity and a time. The other person wants to join but is unavailable then, so they offer one alternative. The first person accepts and states the final activity and time.

sections.title: The same pattern in new situations

spans.value: The structure works with many informal activities.
Lunch with a colleague

no.value: Skal vi spise lunsj sammen på tirsdag klokka tolv?

en.value: Shall we have lunch together on Tuesday at twelve?

no.value: Gjerne, men jeg kan ikke klokka tolv. Hva med klokka ett?

en.value: I’d love to, but I can’t at twelve. How about one?

no.value: Ja, det passer. Da møtes vi i kantina klokka ett.

en.value: Yes, that works. Then we’ll meet in the cafeteria at one.

spans.value: A walk with a friend

no.value: Skal vi gå en tur i kveld?

en.value: Shall we go for a walk tonight?

no.value: Det høres hyggelig ut, men jeg kan ikke før klokka åtte.

en.value: That sounds nice, but I can’t before eight.

no.value: Hva med klokka åtte, da?

en.value: How about eight, then?

no.value: Ja, fint. Da møtes vi ved parken klokka åtte.

en.value: Yes, fine. Then we’ll meet by the park at eight.

spans.value: A film at the weekend

no.value: Hva med å se en film på lørdag?

en.value: How about watching a film on Saturday?

no.value: God idé! Jeg kan ikke på lørdag, men jeg kan på søndag.

en.value: Good idea! I can’t on Saturday, but I’m available on Sunday.

no.value: Søndag passer fint. Da ser vi filmen på søndag.

en.value: Sunday works well. Then we’ll watch the film on Sunday.

spans.value: Without looking back, produce a four-part informal planning exchange: propose an activity, respond to the suggested time, offer one alternative, and state the agreed plan. Use a new activity and make the final sentence clear enough that both people know what they are doing and when.

prompt.value: Choose the meaning that shows what Mina suggests and the activity and time she mentions.

options.text: Mina spør om den avtalte gåturen etter jobb fortsatt gjelder, og Jonas bekrefter avtalen.
options.why: De har ikke avtalt en tur ennå, så Mina spør ikke om en eksisterende avtale.

options.text: Mina foreslår at de går en tur etter jobb, og Jonas takker ja.
options.why: «Skal vi …?» foreslår en aktivitet sammen som Jonas kan takke ja eller nei til.

options.text: Mina sier at Jonas må gå en tur etter jobb, og han godtar kravet.
options.why: Ingenting tyder på at Mina kan pålegge Jonas å gå tur; de er venner.

options.text: Mina forteller at hun har bestemt seg for å gå en tur etter jobb.
options.why: Mina spør om en felles aktivitet i stedet for bare å fortelle om sin egen plan.

text.value: Mina og Jonas snakker om hva de kan gjøre etter jobb.
«Skal vi gå en tur etter jobb?»

prompt.value: You want to get coffee, but you are helping your sister then. Reply that you want coffee but cannot meet at two. Do not suggest another time.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate only the visible reply task. Report verdicts for activity-accepted, time-unavailable, no-alternative-time, and cooperative-language-observation. The first three criteria are gating. Any criterion whose id ends in «-observation» is diagnostic and must not fail an otherwise valid reply. Anchors: PASS: «Ja, gjerne! Jeg vil gjerne ta en kaffe, men jeg kan ikke klokka to.» PASS: «Ja, gjerne! Jeg hjelper søsteren min da, så klokka to passer ikke.» FAIL time-unavailable: «Ja, gjerne! Klokka to passer fint.»

criteria.instruction: The reply communicates that the writer wants to join the coffee plan.
The reply communicates that the writer cannot meet at two o'clock, for example by saying they are busy or unavailable.
The reply does not propose a different time or day; it accepts the coffee plan and explains the conflict without suggesting a replacement.
Observation only: note whether the reply uses a warm or cooperative tone; this is diagnostic only.

text.value: «Skal vi ta en kaffe på lørdag klokka to?»

prompt.value: You would like to come, but you work on Saturday morning. You are free on Sunday afternoon. Reply to Nora: say yes to the walk, say that Saturday does not work, and suggest Sunday.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate only the visible reply task. Report verdicts for accepts-walk, saturday-unavailable, one-sunday-alternative, and alternative-form-observation. The first three criteria are gating. Any criterion whose id ends in «-observation» is diagnostic and must not fail an otherwise valid reply. Anchors: PASS: «Jeg blir gjerne med, men jeg jobber lørdag formiddag. Kan vi gå søndag ettermiddag i stedet?» FAIL one-sunday-alternative: «Jeg blir gjerne med, men jeg kan ikke på lørdag. Kanskje en annen gang.» PASS with alternative-form-observation flagged: «Turen høres hyggelig ut. Jeg jobber lørdag formiddag, men søndag ettermiddag passer for meg.»

criteria.instruction: The reply communicates that the writer wants to join the walk.
The reply communicates that Saturday morning is unavailable.
The reply offers Sunday afternoon as exactly one alternative time.
Observation only: note whether the alternative is framed as a proposal rather than a bare statement; this is diagnostic only.

text.value: «Skal vi gå en tur på lørdag formiddag?»

prompt.value: Write a message exchange in Norwegian between Ada and Leo. Ada suggests going to the cinema on Saturday at 6 p.m. Leo would like to come, but he is working then. He is free on Sunday at 7 p.m. Ada agrees and confirms the cinema plan at Kino Nova on Sunday at 7 p.m. End with Ada confirming the plan.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate only the visible message task. Report verdicts for initial-cinema-proposal, leo-time-problem, one-alternative, final-cinema-confirmation, and target-forms-observation. The first four criteria are gating. Any criterion whose id ends in «-observation» is diagnostic and must not fail an otherwise valid exchange. Anchors: PASS: «Ada: Skal vi gå på Kino Nova på lørdag klokka seks? Leo: Gjerne, men jeg jobber da. Hva med søndag klokka sju? Ada: Ja, det passer. Da ser vi filmen på Kino Nova søndag klokka sju.» FAIL final-cinema-confirmation: «Ada: Skal vi gå på kino lørdag klokka seks? Leo: Jeg jobber da. Hva med søndag klokka sju? Ada: Ja, fint.» PASS with target-forms-observation flagged: «Ada: Kino Nova lørdag klokka seks? Leo: Det vil jeg, men jeg jobber. Søndag klokka sju passer. Ada: Avtale. Vi ser film på Kino Nova søndag klokka sju.»

criteria.instruction: Ada proposes going to the cinema on Saturday at 18:00.
Leo communicates that he wants to join but works at the initially proposed time.
Leo offers Sunday at 19:00 as exactly one alternative.
Ada accepts and clearly confirms the cinema plan for Sunday at 19:00, restating the activity, place, day, and time.
Observation only: note whether the exchange uses the practiced proposal and confirmation patterns; this is diagnostic only.

prompt.value: Write a message exchange between Sara and Amir. Sara suggests bowling at Lucky Strike on Thursday at 7 p.m. Amir would like to come, but he has an evening class then. He suggests Friday at 6 p.m. Sara agrees and confirms the activity, place, day, and time.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate only the visible message task. Report verdicts for bowling-proposal, class-conflict, one-alternative, final-bowling-plan, and practiced-language-observation. The first four criteria are gating. Any criterion whose id ends in «-observation» is diagnostic and must not fail an otherwise valid exchange. PASS: «Sara: Skal vi bowle på Lucky Strike på torsdag klokka sju? Amir: Gjerne, men jeg har undervisning da. Hva med fredag klokka seks? Sara: Ja, det passer. Da bowler vi på Lucky Strike på fredag klokka seks.»

criteria.instruction: Sara proposes bowling at Lucky Strike on Thursday at 19:00.
Amir communicates that he wants to join but has an evening class at the proposed time.
Amir suggests one alternative time, Friday at 18:00, for the same bowling plan.
Sara accepts and clearly confirms bowling at Lucky Strike on Friday at 18:00, restating the activity, place, day, and time.
Observation only: note whether the exchange uses the practiced proposal and confirmation patterns; this is diagnostic only.

prompt.value: Choose the meaning that matches Jonas's reply.

options.text: Jonas vil være med på kaffen, og tidspunktet passer ham.
options.why: Han sier at klokka tre er uaktuell, så tidspunktet er ikke akseptert.

options.text: Jonas vil ikke være med på kaffen, men tidspunktet passer ham.
options.why: «Kaffen er jeg med på» viser at han sier ja til kaffen.

options.text: Jonas vil være med på kaffen og foreslår et nytt tidspunkt.
options.why: Han nevner ikke noe nytt tidspunkt i denne dialogen.

options.text: Jonas vil være med på kaffen, men tidspunktet passer ikke for ham.
options.why: «Kaffen er jeg med på» viser at han sier ja til kaffen, mens «uaktuell» viser at tidspunktet ikke passer.

text.value: «Skal vi ta en kaffe på fredag klokka tre?»
«Kaffen er jeg med på, men klokka tre er uaktuell for meg.»

prompt.value: Choose the reply that keeps the activity and suggests one possible alternative.

options.text: Nei, jeg vil ikke gå en tur. Men søndag ettermiddag passer.
options.why: Den avviser selve turen, som Emil gjerne vil være med på.

options.text: Gjerne, men jeg kan ikke da. Kanskje en annen gang.
Gjerne, men lørdag formiddag passer ikke. Hva med søndag ettermiddag?
options.why: Den beholder turen, avviser bare den opptatte tiden og gir ett konkret alternativ.

options.text: Gjerne! Hva med søndag ettermiddag eller lørdag kveld?
options.why: Den gir flere alternativer, men Emil er bare ledig søndag ettermiddag.

text.value: «Skal vi gå en tur på lørdag formiddag?»
Emil vil gjerne bli med. Han jobber lørdag formiddag, men er ledig søndag ettermiddag.

prompt.value: Choose the reply that confirms the plan without changing it.

options.text: Flott! Da møtes vi på kafeen søndag klokka sju.
options.why: Den bekrefter dagen og klokkeslettet, men flytter møtet fra Kino Nova til en kafé.

options.text: Flott! Da møtes vi på Kino Nova søndag klokka sju.
options.why: Den bekrefter avtalt aktivitet, sted, dag og klokkeslett uten å endre dem.

options.text: Søndag passer, men jeg kommer først klokka åtte.
options.why: Den endrer klokkeslettet fra sju til åtte.

options.text: Gjerne! Da ses vi fredag klokka sju på Kino Nova.
options.why: Den endrer avtalt dag fra søndag til fredag.
